sources.title: Embassy of Panama: immigration and visas
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Panamanian Government embassy immigration page publishes a named no-visa visitor-country list and includes Malta, separately from conditional third-country visa or residence routes.
sources.supportingExcerpt: No Visa RequireD: IF you are from any of the following countries ... Malta

sources.title: Iraq Ministry of Foreign Affairs: obtaining an entry visa upon arrival
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Iraq
sources.officialityEvidence: Iraq's Foreign Ministry consular guidance expressly includes European Union passports in its arrival-visa cohort, describes border issuance and separately advises pre-travel eVisa use from 1 March 2025.
sources.supportingExcerpt: European Union countries ... are granted a visa to Iraq upon arrival through the border crossings.

policies.title: Maltese ordinary passports: Panama short-visit visa exemption
policies.summary: Panama's current embassy immigration guidance names Malta in its no-visa visitor-country list for stays of up to three months.
conditions: Ordinary Maltese passport holder, visitor stay of up to three months; carry the stated passport validity, return/onward travel and funds where requested.
Employment, residence, transit, conditional third-country visa or residence routes, special passports and final admission remain separate.

policies.title: Maltese ordinary passports: Iraq visitor visa issued at arrival
policies.summary: Iraq's current Foreign Ministry guidance includes European Union passports in its visitor visa-on-arrival cohort, which includes ordinary Maltese passports.
conditions: Ordinary Maltese passport holder; the visa is issued at Iraqi land, air or sea border crossings and is stated as valid for 60 days.
Iraq separately advises, but does not require in place of this route, pre-travel eVisa use. Work, residence, special passports, Iraqi-origin treatment and final admission remain separate.

conflicts.explanation: The fallback labels Iraq eVisa, but Iraq's current Foreign Ministry explicitly grants the named European Union passport cohort a visa at arrival; its separate eVisa advice does not eliminate border issuance.
